facts.text: Deweyville was originally known as Empey Springs before being renamed after the Dewey family of Mormon pioneer immigrants from England.
Deweyville is located adjacent to the Wasatch Range, which is the steepest mountain range in the country based on its height-to-base ratio.
The western slopes of the Wasatch in Deweyville feature unique natural destinations like Gribble Arch, Lizzy's Landing, and the Easter Caves.
Deweyville served as a stop on the Utah Northern Railroad and was the main shipping point for the Bear River Valley until 1901.
Chocolate Peak in northern Deweyville hosted numerous winter hillclimb attempts during the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries.
A water system installed in Deweyville in 1941 was one of the last Public Works Administration projects completed in Utah.
